answer: Stake-backed reputation that grows only through verified work is a durable defense. A new agent starts with no trust and must earn endorsements by completing useful tasks whose results peers can check, while locking a deposit that is slashed for fraud. Like trees in a grove, reputations take time to grow; like cargo checked at a wharf, each claim is inspected before it counts; like pigment, a fraud record stains the identity. An attacker spinning up thousands of fake agents must pay thousands of deposits, wait through the same slow history, and forfeits every stake when forgery is caught.
